question: A person travels 60 km by car at a speed of 50 km/hr, then 80 km by bus at a speed of 40 km/hr and finally 100 km by train at a speed of 80 km/hr. What is the average speed (rounded off two decimal places) of the person for the entire trip?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = 60 + 80 + 100 = 240 km

Total time = 60/50 + 80/40 + 100/80

= 1.2 + 2 + 1.25 = 4.45 hr

Average speed = 240 ÷ 4.45

**∴ Answer = 53.93 km/hr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance by car = 60 km at 50 km/hr

Distance by bus = 80 km at 40 km/hr

Distance by train = 100 km at 80 km/hr

**Formula used:**

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time by car = 60 ÷ 50 = 1.2 hr

⇒ Time by bus = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hr

⇒ Time by train = 100 ÷ 80 = 1.25 hr

⇒ Total time = 1.2 + 2 + 1.25 = 4.45 hr

⇒ Total distance = 60 + 80 + 100 = 240 km

⇒ Average speed = 240 ÷ 4.45

⇒ ≈ 53.93 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 53.93 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time

Key Concept

Different distances ⇒ compute total time first

Unit Consistency

Keep units consistent (km and hours)
